[WP] You have always been able to sense Superhumans. This morning, you sensed something strange. What appears to be a normal human has killed a Rank A+ Superhuman...

Three pinprick pressures in my head. Three superhumans. One was unfamiliar, causing a kind of electric numbness on my left cheek that was impossible to ignore. The last time I ever felt something this strong was when I was at a sideline for a parade featuring Hoplite, who could manipulate the volume, size, and even density of any steel object he was holding. I've been to almost all superhuman celebrity appearances, and each was fresh in my memory. I could only count three Heroes who could emanate a sensation that could match what I was feeling in intensity. There was another one, but thinking about it made my right ring finger and pinky to freeze up. I preferred not to recall that one.

I opened my eyes and took a sip of the coffee the secretary has left me. I was in for an interview with Mrs. Fujikawa, an obscure veteran federal agent in the Supernatural Department who, according to some of my sources, was part of a vanguard investigation team, first to arrive in every cases of "unforeseen accidents of large scale". I usually arrive 5 minutes early to a meeting, as the news industry drilled the "on time is late, early is on time" mentality into me, but I made an exception to this particular meeting to be waiting 20 minutes before schedule. I decided that any more would come off as trying too hard to impress.

I was slowly regretting that decision as one of knees began bobbing and fiddling with the tape recorder, a bad habit of mine. It was too easy to become bored in a room where there was only a table and two chairs. I already noted that all the furniture were plain and undecorative, yet not cheap. There was no window I could look out from. In a glance, my watch told me it was 11 minutes before the meeting.

Nevertheless to say, it surprised me when the door opened with Mrs. Fujikawa striding in. It's almost never the case that someone in an obviously higher position inconvenience themselves for the sake of the other. I was just a reporter trying to climb the corporate ladder. I instantly straightened my spine.

"I hope you haven't been waiting long." She said, as she took her seat closest to the door, a position she was left with as I took the more humble option.

I shook my head, trying to hide that I was feeling nervous, and physically uncomfortable on the face. It was really weird trying to smile when you can't feel certain muscles. "No ma'am."

She gave me a smile that tilted the edge of her lips ever so slightly and briefly disappeared. She had enough wrinkles to convince me she was at least five more years than what her birth date indicated, although she didn't seem to have any grey hair. I caught myself staring. Damn amateur mistake. This was far from being my first professional interview, but I couldn't help but feel like it was.

"Well, Mrs. Fujikawa, I have a few questions to start us off ..." I trailed off as she raised her hand.

She then dug into her suit pocket and withdrew a red button. One just like those Staples Easy button, except without text. I was speechless for a moment. This did pissed me off a little, but I couldn't afford to accuse her of anything yet.

She slid it across me. I didn't want to trigger some sort of faux pas, so I waited.

"I want you to press it."

Straight to the damn point, wasn't she.

I didn't bother trying to force a natural smile and reached over to lay my index finger on the button and pressed it with a tinge of spite.

My left cheek didn't feel numb anymore.

I rubbed it just to make sure.

"So you are indeed a D rank." The voice snapped me back to reality.

I could only stare back into the eyes that cooly gazed into mine. The shaking in my chest spread throughout my body, and unfortunately my throat.

"Who was .. this person?"

"Was, not is?" She gave that smile again. "Not someone who deserved to live." She let the comment hang, continuing the mutual staring. "You don't seem surprised, more shocked. So you know how to differentiate teleportation and .. this."

I didn't know what to say in response, and I ended up becoming tight lipped. She continued to talk.

"I'm sure several of your colleagues told you that I am a detective, or someone who checks the aftermath wreck for evidences. They are half right. That is indeed part of my work. However," She gave a sigh. "that only comes when I fail my main duty."

I couldn't keep up the eye contact. I had to lower my gaze, keeping silent.

"There isn't a need to feel guilty. The murder is not on your hands." She looked at the button. "Irony aside."

"But somehow you felt the need to kill ... " Someone that must have been difficult as hell to capture, or kill. Trading a A+ rank for a D. "Why?"

"Why indeed?" She wanted me to answer.

I knew why, and made my shaking worse.

[WP] As a servant of Death, you have powers proportionally related to the amount of souls you take per day. Today, you encountered your first immortal.

I stared at the being in front of me and it stared back at me. Its ancient eyes traced the contours and etchings of my mask. I wondered what false image it saw in place of me. The mask would give the illusion of a being's perception of death, a skeleton, a beast, or a god, but for this one... I wasn't sure. Whatever it was seeing and whether it could see it, the being did not give any indication. The being watched me, studying me, as if it were taking notes. Slowly, I lowered my gaze and it followed mine to a body resting on its bed. Ancient, but still full of energy, breathing, but living no more, it rested on its bed. Dead and alive. The being still did not seemed bothered by seeing its own body from outside. Of course, perhaps this being wasn't even sure what it seeing. It wasn't supposed to die. Death applied to everyone else, but not it.

I waited for a response, gave it time to process and let it build up a reaction, but nothing of the sort. It leaned over its own body and examined it. Every curve and indentation. Every scar and blemish. It examined it, but it dared not touch its own body, much to my relief. After low hums and short flickers of eye movements, it stood up again.

"I have died, but not quite", it said meeting me with the same gaze again.

"Yes. Your vessel has released your soul, parting you from life's grip"

"I see." it placed a finger on its chin, "You are Death, but not quite"

"I am a servant of Death. I perform some of his duties"

"The mask, it fails you. It tries to make a face, an image of something, but it just doesn't keep it on" It said, coming closer.

It moved unnaturally, even for a spirit. It stared directly past the failed illusion and directly into my own eyes. I sensed its incredible life hidden away behind its own eyes. After holding me in its stare, it promptly broke it and moved slowly away. The being surveyed the room we were in. Taking it anew. It touched the walls and ran its hand from side to side, from top to bottom slowly. It took in the sounds its hand made as it traveled lower until it was stopped by a desk. The being then scanned the top of the desk, eyeing the objects placed on it. Its eyes stopped on a small irregular shape on the corner. It placed its finger on the small object and ran it across the ridges on the surface. The being had a slight smile as it felt the objects physical surface properties. It then wrapped its fingers around the objects and lifted it cleanly off the desk. Shivers ran down my spine as the being effortlessly tossed the object in its hands. Impossible.

"Its a different experience, being dead. Alive, everything blends in, but dead, it is a different matter. Another state of being, another set of experiences. Rare ones too. Everything has meaning when dead. What do you think?"

"I'm not sure what you mean"

"Exactly. I'm always alive, I don't end. I know people who meant something, but only when they've passed on. They left a mark, but me, I leave a trail. Nothing ultimate about it at all"

"I'm not sure what you are saying"

"Ah, I might just be rambling. I'm probably just old now" The being said, tossing the object towards me. It curved in an arc and as it reached its peak, it slowed down and halted in space.

The being turned its back on me to investigate the desk once again. I reached for the object suspended in space and tried to nudge it from its position, but did not move. I applied more force, but it was locked in its position in the air. I stepped to the side, away from the objects future arc and watched the being continue being dead. It made its way to the other side of the room, touching, feeling and occasionally moving stationary objects. Everytime, it would send my soul into a state of terror. Everytime, impossible.

"So why you?" the being asked.

"Why me, what?" I replied.

"I'm immortal. Many have tried to take my soul and all have surrendered the cause. All but you. So, again, why you? Why are you here?"

"It is my duty. A being dies and I am to take their soul when they pass"

"Except, I am immortal. I do not pass"

"It is possible you may have changed your mind"

"Do you believe that is a possibility?"

"With you, it is minimal, but still possible, so I came, just incase"

"Just incase?"

"Just incase"

It walked closer to me, kicking a few dropped items out of the way as it did. It had its hands behind its back as it circled me. I kept still, allowing myself to be viewed by the being. It nodded and murmured barely audible words to itself. With those ancient eyes, it could see my true form, of that I was sure. Then, it stopped and spoke.

"I am eons old." it started, "I've forgotten names and I've forgotten mine. The lives I live, blur into eachother. Each without beginning nor end. I continue to exist, but I forget why I do. I've done all I've ever needed to do with my first life and even more so by my second. I have no regrets. These limitless years have given me opportunity to fix any mistake I've commited. No consequences or rewards. I just continue to exist and I think, I am tired of that. I'm tired of wandering. Of being"

My soul shuddered in my vessel hearing those last words

"Are you sure?"

"Of that, I am sure. I am tired and I've been tired for a long time"

"If you are ready, I can take you"

The being looked at me one more time. Its eyes looking me up and down one final time before being fixed on mine. I could see the sincerity in its eyes. How tired it really was.

"Next time"

"Next time?" I asked confused.

"Yes. Next time. Not just yet" the being said, dismissing me with a wave of its hand. "I think it would be best if I said goodbye to everyone before I go. I missed my opportunity this time. So next time, I'll do it properly. I'll go then."

My shoulders sagged slightly. I'm sure the being could see my dissapointment, but it did not aknowledge it. It simply moved back beside its body and knelt beside it.

"Next time. When you are ready. I will wait."

"Yes. Next time." the being said staring longly at its body "Of course".

With that, the being placed its hand on its head and slowly, his soul was returning to its original vessel. The being was firmly in the grasp of life once again. I heard a clunk as the airborn object thrown by the being returned to reality again. The being did not wake immediatly, but stirred slightly in its slumber. I looked for the object thrown and I moved my hands through it. I could feel the energy still residing around it after being moved. Incredible energy. I wanted it. I wanted what it had, what it harbored, but I would have to wait. I'd have to settle for the other souls that part their vessels within a short lifespan. They gave little to me, but an immortal soul, even just a taste left me wanting. I think that reaping an immortal soul may just mean something.

I look at my watch on my left hand. It is 48 minutes, and 30ish seconds away from midnight. Today's harvest was on a fruitful end, though relatively. It's paltry compared to the choleric outbreaks days, but I'll take what I can get. Advancing medicine and relative peace made deaths more concentrated in hospitals, and the big wigs already claimed them as territory. It's infuriating to have to scavenge elsewhere, but complaining about it gets no one anywhere.

Speaking of getting somewhere, I look at my compass on my right hand. It didn't tell the distance, which made the winding roads of Edinburgh especially debilitating to navigating to the destination. But I was no stranger to sidestepping perpendicularly and pinpointing the location of the freshest release of life by noticing the minuscule difference in direction. It had taken a century of practice to get this down right, but I had patience. Scarcity demanded adaptation, and adapt I did.

I kept a brisk walk on the cobblestone roads, sidestepping along the way to get a hold of where I needed to go. Running would only attract attention from fellow coworkers, and anonymity was valuable. I also had the ability to control impulsiveness, a quality that most others lacked, whom were either arrogantly powerful, or gone for good.

I stopped in front of an old, paint-peeling two-story house with a rather unkempt fenced garden. I move left and right, seemingly pondering, while glancing at my compass. Confirming, I walked up the porch, looking around to see no one was around this dreary night, and phased through the door.

Inside, I had little reason to hide my incorporeal nature, and I looked into each rooms, but no departed soul. I went upstairs and did the same, with no result. Even the bathrooms were empty. I finally found a hidden door to the attic, and climbed right through it.

The first few things I saw were the typical boxes and objects, some paintings, covered in cloth. But what I saw next surprised me.

"And that, my lady, is a servant of Death, though I prefer to call them wraiths."

There were two bodies, and two anchored souls. A pair of together deceased. Incredibly unusual to see now a days. What was more perplexing was that they were vastly different from each other in most aspects, but not in a way that made them opposites. One was a woman, the other ... questionably male. She was distinctively local Scottish in appearance and he was ... not even English, not completely Orient either. Whole contrasted with ... dense.

The continuing silence broke into my attention. I tried to hide my loss of composure with my next words.

"Excuse me?"

Damn

I coughed, recovering my usual poker face and taking in the situation anew. The man, or his soul, was standing with his arms behind him, collected, like a host with authority. The specter of the lady sat at one of the stray chair, cordial, like a polite audience.

The man spoke. "You are here absorb us, aren't you?"

I narrowed my eyes at him. "I'm afraid you're wrong. I am here to collect you."

He gave a smile. "Euphemisms."

I turned to the lady. She wore a straight face, confident in manner, but I saw one of her hand wringing at her dress. I reached out a hand toward her.

"Ma'am, I assure you, whatever this man told you about death and the afterlife, I am at greater authority in its matter."

He gave a grin. "Then what is the afterlife after you whisk them away?"

I opened my mouth, but didn't know what to say. I closed it. It came to me that I had no obligation to entertain them. I took out my watch. "I'm sorry, but I don't have all the time in the world. I must get to business."

I reached out to him and prepared the utterance, to release the soul from his physical body for his given time has past and spent, thus ...

Not a single word escaped my mouth.

"Let's talk about your business." He dropped his grin, but still wearing that cocky smile. "I promised this lady to give her a proper explanation on how to be immortal."

I don't remember strategies for IV, so I'm basing this off my experience with Civ V, but it's still applicable IMO. I always lose on deity though, the highest I can do is immortal.

You can't really effectively take cities until the medieval era, since an early game war will kill your infrastructure development. The best strategy is to turtle up and try to get a science lead, while sabotaging your neighbors by stealing their workers and bribing them to declare war on each other. By the time you have crossbowmen(V)/musketmen(IV) you can start to take land as long as you don't fall behind in science.
